                Defendants.

      PLAINTIFF'S MOTION FOR ENTRY OF A SCHEDULING ORDER AND, AS
 NECESSARY, AN INITIAL PRETRIAL CONFERENCE UNDER FEDERAL RULE OF
                CIVIL PROCEDURE 16(b) AND LOCAL CIVIL RULE 16(B)


        PlaintiffMarvelle J. Ballentine moves under Federal Rule of Civil Procedure 16(b)(l)-(3)

 and Local Civil Rule 16(B) for three forms of relief. First, Plaintiff requests entry of a scheduling

 order after the report or consultation that Rule 16(b)(1) requires. Second, Plaintiff requests an

 initial pretrial conference if one is necessary to obtain that consultation. Third, if either step is

 postponed, Plaintiff requests that the order state the good cause found under Rule 16(b)(2) and the

 date or event on which scheduling will next be addressed. Under Local Civil Rule 7(F), a

 supporting memorandum and a proposed order accompany this Motion.




                                                   1

 I.       GROUNDS
          1.    The action is pending. The operative pleading is the First Amended Complaint.

 ECF 5. ECF 84 denied Plaintiffs motion for leave to amend. ECF 84 at 1-2. Applications

 challenging that denial remain pending. The action is not without an operative pleading.

          2.    The events that start the Rule 16(b)(2) period have occurred. Defendant National

 Center for Missing & Exploited Children ("NCMEC") was served on July 31, 2026. ECF 3.

 NCMEC appeared on August 12, 2026, by filing its motion to dismiss. ECF 10.

          3.    The ordinary Rule 16(b)(2) deadline, absent a finding of good cause for delay,

 was October 13, 2026. Sixty days after August 12, 2026 was Sunday, October 11, 2026. Monday,

 October 12, 2026 was Columbus Day. The period ran to Tuesday, October 13, 2026. Fed. R. Civ.

 P. 6(a)(l)(C), 6(a)(6)(A), 16(b)(2). The memorandum shows the computation.

          4.    No scheduling order has been entered. The docket through ECF 101 contains no

 Rule 16(b) scheduling order. ECF 84 stated on October 7, 2026 that "currently there is no

 Scheduling Order in this case." ECF 84 at 1-2.

          5.    The parties' conference under Rule 26(f) is the subject of a separate motion. This

 Motion does not depend on the disposition of that motion, and that motion does not depend on the

 disposition of this one. Rule 16(b)(1 )(B) supplies a route to the scheduling order that does not

 require a completed Rule 26(f) report.

          6.    This Motion does not rest on any Defendant's conduct. Plaintiff seeks a

 scheduling order because the Rule 16(b)(2) period has run and the action is not exempt from Rule

 16(b).

          7.    This Motion does not claim that passage of the scheduling deadline itself

 authorizes service of discovery. It does not claim that the lapse affects the Court's jurisdiction or

 the validity of any order entered since.


                                                  2

Case 1:26-cv-02331-RDA-WEF              Document 103        Filed 10/28/26       Page 3 of 7 PageID#
                                              1053



 II.    SCOPE
         8.     This Motion seeks initial case management. It does not seek enforcement of

 Plaintiffs Rule 26(f) proposals, authorization of particular discovery, sanctions, or reconsideration

 of any prior order. The pending applications challenging the amendment and discovery denials

 and addressing the reassignment remain presented on their own grounds. No request is withdrawn

 by this Motion.

 III.   RELIEF REQUESTED
        9.      Entry of the scheduling order. Plaintiff requests that the Court:

        (a)     set a Rule 16(b) scheduling conference on a date certain within 21 days after entry

 of the order granting this Motion, unless a sufficient Rule 26(f) report filed before that date permits

 entry of the scheduling order without a conference;

        (b)     enter the scheduling order at the conference or within seven days after it, limiting

 the time to join other parties, amend the pleadings, complete discovery, and file motions, Fed. R.

 Civ. P. 16(b)(3)(A), and fixing the discovery cut-off, the final pretrial conference date, and, where

 practicable, the trial date, Local Civil Rule 16(B); and

        (c)     shorten the preparatory intervals under Fed. R. Civ. P. 26(f)(l) and 26(£)(4) and

 Local Civil Rule 26(A)(l), so that the parties confer no later than seven days before the Court's

 conference and file a written Rule 26(f) report no later than three days before it, with oral reporting

 only if the Court excuses the written report. Plaintiff requests that the conference-setting order

 select dates that can be met after the order issues.

         10.    Independent request for an initial conference. If the Court determines that entry of

 the complete scheduling order should await disposition of a pending matter, Plaintiff separately

 requests that the Court determine whether an initial scheduling conference can proceed now to

 establish the remaining case-management steps.



                                                    3

Case 1:26-cv-02331-RDA-WEF            Document 103        Filed 10/28/26      Page 4 of 7 PageID#
                                            1054



        11.     Disposition upon postponement. If the Court postpones either the scheduling

 conference or entry of the scheduling order, Plaintiff requests that the order state the good cause

 found under Rule 16(b)(2) and the date or event on which scheduling will next be addressed.

        12.     This alternative request does not constitute agreement that further postponement

 is warranted and does not withdraw the request for scheduling now.

        13.     The proposed 21-day, seven-day, and three-day periods are requested case-

 management terms. The rules do not impose them.
